name: Iranun
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source, which also states the stress rule; 10 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

International Journal of Research Studies in Education 11(14) (Special IJRSE Luminary Issue): 43-48. Consortia Academia Publishing. DOI 10.5861/ijrse.2022.b015. (In Filipino; Western Mindanao State University.)
catalog_quote: malinaw na ang wikang Iranun ay nagtataglay din ng mga salita na pareho ang baybay ngunit iba ang kahulugan ayon sa diin gaya ng salitang, lima [‘li.ma] na nangangahulugang kamay at lima [li.’ma] na nangangahulugang bilang. … Ang malumay ay binibigkas nang mabagal ngunit walang impit na tunog at ang diin ng salita ay makikita sa ikalawang pantig mula sa hulihan ng salita.

tone_statements.citation: Toto, Sitti Aisha G. & Aubrey F. Reyes. 2022. Pagsusuri sa ponemang suprasegmental ng wikang Iranun [An analysis of the suprasegmental phonemes of the Iranun language]. International Journal of Research Studies in Education 11(14) (Special IJRSE Luminary Issue): 43-48. Consortia Academia Publishing. (In Filipino; Western Mindanao State University.)
tone_statements.quote: Ang wikang Iranun ay nagtataglay din ng tono o pagbabago sa kahulugan ng isang o pahayag ayon sa pagtaas at pagbaba ng tinig. … Mapapansin sa mga halimbawang binigay na nagbabago ang kahulugan ng isang pangungusap o parirala ayon sa tono ng pagbigkas gaya ng halimbawa 1.a. ang unang halimbawa ay nagsasaad na ang taong nagsasalita ay nagtatanong sa kanyang kausap. … Ang pagtaas ng tinig kapag nagtatanong ang mga taal na Iranun ay makikita sa unang salitang ng pangungusap, ang … salitang anda, susundan ng pagbaba ng tinig sa salitang kag at katamtamang pagtaas naman ng tinig sa salitang sung.
tone_statements.translation: The Iranun language also has tone, i.e. a change in the meaning of a [sentence] or utterance according to the rising and falling of the voice. ... It can be seen in the examples given that the meaning of a sentence or phrase changes according to the tone of pronunciation, as in example 1.a: the first example indicates that the speaker is asking his interlocutor a question. ... The rise of the voice when native Iranun ask a question is seen on the first word of the sentence, the word anda, followed by a fall of the voice on the word kag and a moderate rise of the voice on the word sung.
tone_statements.locator: p. 46, sec. 4 'Diskusyon', last two paragraphs, continuing to top of p. 47; examples = Talahanayan 4 'Tono ng wikang Iranun', p. 45

sources.citation: Allison, E. Joe. 1979. Proto-Danaw: a comparative study of Maranaw, Magindanaw and Iranun. Papers in Philippine Linguistics No. 10 (Pacific Linguistics A-55), 53-112. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction with Iranun (Philippine Iranun) phoneme data. States that stress for Proto-Danaw 'could not be reconstructed from the data available to me' (p. 69), gives an Iranun rule in which *e > a 'in a stressed penult' (sec. 3.4.2.1, p. 71), and in fn. 11 (p. 104) says stress conditions *e > IRN a but 'data for stress is incomplete and, in many forms, unattested'. No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.note: Ch. 9 is a Maranao phonology (not Iranun): 'Unlike Maguindanaon (Sullivan 1986:11), Maranao does not appear to have phonemic stress contrasts' (p. 286), fn. 3: 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress.' Iranun is mentioned only for consonant-cluster correspondences and a Sabah Iranun wordlist by Pandikar Padi (Kota Belud); no Iranun stress statement.
